| 4 | Moderna | MRNA | mRNA |

| 6 | Genmab | GMAB | Antibody formats |
| 7 | Argenx | ARGX | FcRn antagonist |

---

## Research Dimensions

**Q1. Platform Extensibility Value Score**
Platforms differ in how many "children assets" they can spawn. Compute "extensibility score":
- Patent IP breadth (years remaining on platform IP)
- Indication reachability (how many disease areas platform tech applies to)
- Partnered out-licensing revenue capacity
- Next-gen iteration roadmap
For each platform, rank "spawn capacity" 1-10. Which platforms face near-term obsolescence vs have 10+ years of expansion?

**Q2. Revenue Concentration Adjusted for Platform Dependency**
Vertex has 90% Trikafta concentration but it's within the CFTR platform. Argenx has 100% Vyvgart but on FcRn platform. Compute **"platform-concentration-adjusted" risk**:
- If platform fails (new competitor takes modality), % revenue at risk
- If single product fails (ADEs, LOE), % revenue at risk
Separate single-product vs platform risk. Which biotech has most **platform-diversified** revenue?

**Q3. Royalty Structure Optimization**
For each royalty stream: (a) royalty % tier, (b) duration remaining, (c) triggers (milestone-based vs revenue-based), (d) NPV @ 10% discount. Which biotech has most valuable royalty book per $ market cap?

**Q4. Pipeline PoS-Weighted Value**
For each biotech's pipeline: apply industry-standard Phase transition probabilities (BIO Industry Analysis):
- Phase 1 → Phase 2: 52%
- Phase 2 → Phase 3: 28%
- Phase 3 → Approval: 58%
- Filed → Approval: 88%
Compute expected number of approvals per biotech + aggregate expected NPV at consensus peak sales. Rank by pipeline EV.

**Q5. Cash-to-Pipeline-Value Ratio (Acquirer Math)**
Compute: **(Current Market Cap) - (Sum of Cash + Commercial Asset Value) - (Risk-adjusted pipeline NPV)**. Residual = implied "platform premium". Which biotechs trade at negative platform premium (attractive acquisition math)?

**Q6. Post-COVID Math: Spikevax Tail + New Launch Adoption**
For Moderna + BioNTech:
- Spikevax 2025-27 long tail (assume $1-3B/year stable)
- Non-COVID launches adoption curves (mResvia, RSV Flu combo, autogene cevumeran)
- Cumulative 2027 revenue assuming 25% pipeline success (risk-adjusted)
Which mRNA biotech has faster cliff recovery math?

**Q7. M&A Target Attractiveness: Pharma Buyer Perspective**
For each of Pfizer / Merck / J&J / AbbVie / Lilly / Bristol-Myers (big pharma from Case 05), identify which biotech is most strategically complementary:
- Fills pharma's therapeutic gap
- Within pharma's M&A appetite ($EV manageable)
- No partnership conflict

Produce 6 pharma → biotech "best fit" matches. Justify each.

**Q8. R&D Productivity Per Platform (vs Big Pharma Benchmark)**
Compute: FY20-24 cumulative R&D spend / FY20-24 cumulative novel approvals, per biotech. Compare to Big Pharma baseline (Case 05 answer: AZN 0.27/$B best, PFE 0.11/$B worst). Which biotech has best platform ROI on R&D?

## Assumptions and Source Base

Figures are rounded. Currency is USD unless noted. FX: `EUR/USD = 1.08`; `DKK/USD = 0.145`. Market caps are rounded early-May-2026 screening values from live market-cap pages and current quote context; Q5 is an acquisition-screening model, not a full DCF.

Primary sources used include: Vertex FY2025 results: https://investors.vrtx.com/news-releases/news-release-details/vertex-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial; SEC/company filing pages for Regeneron, Amgen, Moderna, BioNTech, Genmab, Argenx, Alnylam: https://www.sec.gov/edgar/browse/?CIK=872589, https://www.sec.gov/edgar/browse/?CIK=318154, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001682852/000168285226000033/mrna-20251231.htm, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1776985/000177698526000016/ex992bntx4qfy2025present.htm, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1434265/000143426526000014/gmab-20251231_d2.htm, https://reports.argenx.com/2025, https://www.sec.gov/edgar/browse/?CIK=1178670. Phase probabilities use the BIO industry framework supplied in the prompt and checked against BIO’s clinical-development success-rate work: https://www.bio.org/clinical-development-success-rates-and-contributing-factors-2011-2020.

---

## Q1. Platform Extensibility Value Score

| Rank | Entity | Platform | Spawn score /10 | Expansion runway | Key judgment |
|---:|---|---|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Genmab | Antibody formats | 9.0 | 10+ yrs | Best royalty-spawning platform: DuoBody/HexaBody/DuoHexaBody can create partnered oncology/immunology assets without Genmab funding every pivotal trial. |
| 2 | Alnylam | RNAi | 9.0 | 10+ yrs | Broad liver-targeted RNAi, growing extrahepatic optionality, validated repeated-drug model across TTR, complement, metabolic, CNS-adjacent targets. |
| 3 | Regeneron | VelocImmune | 8.5 | 10+ yrs | High-throughput antibody discovery has repeatedly generated Dupixent, Libtayo, rare-disease and oncology assets; strong extensibility but less royalty leverage than Genmab. |
| 4 | BioNTech | mRNA / immuno-oncology | 8.0 | 10+ yrs, oncology-weighted | mRNA plus ADC/bispecific oncology portfolio gives broader post-COVID surface than vaccine-only mRNA; execution risk remains high. |
| 5 | Moderna | mRNA | 7.5 | 7-10+ yrs | Very broad vaccine/therapeutic roadmap, but current commercial validation remains COVID/RSV-heavy and IP/lipid-delivery disputes reduce score. |
| 6 | Amgen | Biologics | 7.0 | 10+ yrs | Durable biologics manufacturing and clinical engine, but “biologics” is less proprietary as a platform and growth increasingly depends on acquired assets. |
| 7 | Argenx | FcRn antagonist | 6.5 | 7-10 yrs | Efgartigimod can spawn many IgG-mediated autoimmune indications, but target-level competition is intense and platform is mostly one molecule/franchise. |
| 8 | Vertex | CFTR modulators | 6.0 | CF runway into late 2030s; narrow spawn field | Excellent CF franchise IP and next-gen iteration, but CFTR is disease-area constrained. Vertex’s non-CF growth depends on separate platforms, not CFTR itself. |

Near-term obsolescence risk is highest for COVID-only mRNA revenue pools, single-target FcRn crowding, and CFTR revenue concentration. The best 10+ year “child-asset factories” are Genmab, Alnylam, Regeneron, and BioNTech.

---

## Q2. Platform-Concentration-Adjusted Revenue Risk

| Entity | FY2025 revenue base | Largest single-product / franchise risk | Platform-risk exposure | Platform-diversification view |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Vertex | Product revenue ~$11.0B; Trikafta/Kaftrio ~$10.2B | ~93% | CFTR products ~99% | Very high product and platform concentration despite excellent franchise quality. |
| Regeneron | Revenue ~$15.9B | Dupixent economics and Eylea family each material, neither 90% | ~50-60% VelocImmune/antibody-linked; rest includes Eylea/other economics | Diversified across immunology, ophthalmology, oncology, rare disease. |
| Amgen | Revenue ~$35.6B | Largest products generally low-teens % | Biologics-related majority, but not one modality target | Most platform-diversified revenue in the group. |
| Moderna | Revenue largely Spikevax tail plus RSV launch | Spikevax ~80-90% | mRNA ~100% | High platform dependency; commercial base still too narrow. |
| BioNTech | FY2025 revenue ~€2.8B | Comirnaty/Pfizer economics majority | mRNA / oncology immunotherapy ~75-85% | Cash-rich, but revenue still COVID-concentrated. |
| Genmab | Revenue ~$3.3B | Darzalex royalties ~70%+ | Antibody formats ~100% | Product-concentrated, but platform has already produced multiple partnered assets. |
| Argenx | VYVGART net product sales ~$3.6B | VYVGART ~95%+ | FcRn ~95%+ | Highest single-product risk with Vertex. |
| Alnylam | Net product revenue ~$2.7B | TTR franchise majority | RNAi ~100% | Platform concentrated, but disease/product breadth is better than Argenx/Vertex. |

Most platform-diversified revenue: **Amgen**, then **Regeneron**. Highest platform-adjusted risk: **Moderna**, **Argenx**, **Vertex**, **Alnylam**.

## Q3. Royalty Structure Optimization

NPV method: `NPV10 = annual royalty × duration factor`, with growth/decay adjusted by asset maturity. Where royalty tiers are not disclosed, I used reported royalty revenue and described the limitation.

| Entity | Main royalty / partner economics | Structure | Duration / trigger | Est. royalty-book NPV @10% | NPV / mkt cap |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Genmab | Darzalex, Kesimpta, Tivdak, Epkinly and antibody-format economics | Darzalex tiered royalty widely disclosed around 12-20%; others include royalties/profit share | Net-sales based, patent/product-life dependent | **$14-17B** | **~80-95%** |
| Alnylam | Novartis Leqvio; Sanofi fitusiran/Qfitlia future royalty | Leqvio royalty tiered up to ~20%; fitusiran disclosed 15-30% range | Net-sales based; portion monetized/financed via Blackstone economics | $2-3B gross; ~$1.5-2.5B net | ~4-7% |
| Regeneron | Bayer Eylea ex-US economics; Sanofi antibody collaboration | Mostly profit-share/collaboration economics, not clean royalties | Revenue/profit based | $5-7B if treated as royalty-like | ~7-10% |
| BioNTech | Pfizer Comirnaty economics | Gross-profit share, not royalty | Product revenue/profit share | $3-4B tail value | ~13-17% |
| Amgen | Mature royalties/licensing in other revenue | Mixed, not fully tier-disclosed | Contract/product based | $2-3B | ~1-2% |
| Argenx | Zai Lab China and smaller partner economics | Territory royalties/milestones | Sales and milestone based | <$0.5B | <2% |
| Vertex | No material recurring royalty book | N/A | N/A | <$0.5B | <1% |
| Moderna | No material royalty-inflow book; pays third-party royalties | N/A | N/A | ~$0 | 0% |

Best royalty book per market cap: **Genmab by a wide margin**. If profit shares are excluded and only classical royalties are counted, Genmab remains first and Alnylam is second.

PoS to approval: Filed `88%`; Phase 3 `58%`; Phase 2 `16.2%`; Phase 1 `8.4%`.

Because asset-level consensus peak sales are not uniformly disclosed, the fallback valuation is: `risk-adjusted NPV ≈ peak sales × 2.5 × PoS × ownership`, cross-checked against company pipeline stage disclosures.

| Rank | Entity | Main value drivers | Expected approvals | Risk-adjusted pipeline NPV |
|---:|---|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | Amgen | MariTide obesity, rocatinlimab, olpasiran, bemarituzumab, Imdelltra expansion | ~4.0 | **$30-35B** |
| 2 | Regeneron | Itepekimab, fianlimab/cemiplimab, odronextamab, linvoseltamab, pozelimab/cemdisiran, obesity antibody combinations | ~4.5-5.0 | **$22-28B** |
| 3 | BioNTech | BNT327/PD-L1xVEGF, ADCs, individualized cancer vaccines, later-stage oncology combinations | ~3.0 | **$14-18B** |
| 4 | Argenx | Efgartigimod indication expansion, empasiprubart, ARGX-119 | ~3.0 | **$12-16B** |
| 5 | Alnylam | Zilebesiran, cemdisiran, mivelsiran/ALN-APP, TTR next gen | ~2.2 | **$10-14B** |
| 6 | Vertex | Povetacicept, zimislecel, inaxaplin, VX-522, pain follow-ons | ~2.5 | **$9-12B** |
| 7 | Genmab | Acasunlimab, epcoritamab expansions, rinatabart sesutecan, next-gen DuoBody assets | ~2.4 | **$8-12B** |
| 8 | Moderna | CMV, flu, COVID/flu combo, norovirus, INT oncology with Merck | ~2.5-3.0 | **$8-11B** |

Highest pipeline EV: **Amgen**, mainly because even one obesity/metabolic success is very large. Best platform-style pipeline optionality per dollar of market cap: **BioNTech, Moderna, Genmab, Alnylam**.

Residual formula: `Market cap - cash - commercial asset value - risk-adjusted pipeline NPV`.

| Entity | Mkt cap | Cash / investments | Commercial asset value | Pipeline rNPV | Residual platform premium |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Vertex | ~$105B | ~$11B | ~$88B | ~$11B | **~-$5B** |
| Regeneron | ~$70B | ~$19B | ~$55B | ~$25B | **~-$29B** |
| Amgen | ~$160B | ~$8B | ~$120B | ~$32B | **~$0B** |
| Moderna | ~$13B | ~$6B | ~$4B | ~$9B | **~-$6B** |
| BioNTech | ~$23B | ~$17B | ~$4B | ~$16B | **~-$14B** |
| Genmab | ~$18B | ~$4.5B | ~$18B | ~$10B | **~-$14.5B** |
| Argenx | ~$38B | ~$3B | ~$34B | ~$15B | **~-$14B** |

## Q6. Post-COVID Math: Moderna vs BioNTech

Assumption requested: Spikevax tail stabilizes at `$1-3B/year`. I used midpoint-ish COVID tails plus 25% risk-adjusted contribution for not-yet-approved launches.

Metric shown both ways because the prompt says spend/approval, while the benchmark comparison uses approvals per `$B`. Big Pharma baseline supplied: AZN best `0.27 approvals/$B`; PFE worst `0.11 approvals/$B`.

|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | Genmab | ~$5.1B | ~6 | **1.18** | ~$0.85B | Best platform ROI; partner-funded antibody formats create approvals efficiently. |
